title: Angela Merici (27 January)
hookLine: she founded the Ursulines, women who stayed in their own homes and taught girls

lines: TWO DOORS: MARRIAGE OR A CONVENT.
cards: In an Italian city, a group of young women want to give their whole lives to God. In their world, that usually meant one of two doors: marriage, or a convent behind a wall.

A convent often meant a dowry, and some of them had nothing to bring; others had parents who needed them at home. An older woman named Angela, with no money and no title, opened a third door. Stay where you are.
Live in your own homes. Belong to God anyway. And teach the girls of this city.

teach.b: Angela grew up near Lake Garda in northern Italy and lost her parents young. She lived simply, as a laywoman connected to the Franciscans, and later settled in Brescia, where people came to her for advice.
Tradition says that as a young woman she saw a ladder reaching up to heaven, with young women climbing it, and understood she would one day gather a community.
In Brescia, she did: the Company of Saint Ursula, named for a legendary martyr who led a band of young women. The members took no vows in a cloister and at first wore no habit.
They stayed with their families, met together, prayed, and taught girls the faith: holiness without the wall, carried into ordinary homes.
Angela left her companions a Rule, some Counsels and a Testament, and what stands out is how much room she left.

teach.h: CHANGE THE RULE IF TIMES CHANGE.
teach.b: If times and needs changed, she told the leaders after her, they should make new rules or change things, carefully and with good advice. And things did change.
After her death the Ursulines became religious sisters running schools, often within convents, and Ursuline schools spread.
But it began with a woman and a handful of companions who refused to believe a girl's education could wait.
Luke tells of Mary, Martha's sister, sitting at Jesus's feet to listen, a woman taking her place as a learner, and Jesus defending it.

teach.h: MARY HATH CHOSEN THE BEST PART.
teach.b: In the Douay-Rheims: "Mary hath chosen the best part, which shall not be taken away from her." Some readers hear Angela's whole work in that line.

how: Catholics keep Saint Angela Merici's memorial in January, and Ursuline sisters and schools around the world celebrate her as their founder.

games.q: you're Angela. young women want to give their lives to God, but some can't bring a dowry and some are needed at home. what do you do?
o: raise money to found a new convent for them.
help them stay home, live consecrated lives, and teach girls.
tell them marriage is the only realistic path.
games.why: she founded the Company of Saint Ursula: women living in their own homes, belonging to God, teaching girls.

practice: Bring to mind one girl you know, a daughter, a niece, a student, or the girl you once were, and ask what she's learning now and what would help her keep going: a book, a ride to class, a word that she's smart.
If you pray, ask Angela Merici to pray for her by name; if you don't, just hold her name.

wordCard.voice: Angela Merici. The founder of the Company of Saint Ursula, women who lived consecrated lives in their own homes and taught girls the faith.

carryVoice: Your line: teach the girls. A third door, opened right at home. See you tomorrow.
